gen-dafont-galaxy-gf-lexend-zetta: Galaxy's dense, tall lowercase band and loose letterfit give it a cosmic, commanding pull from the first line. And Lexend Zetta takes the quieter job, widely tracked sans-serif cut like ribbon, so the two share the page easily.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-cascadia-code: Groovy squeezes its c almost shut, loosely tracked and friendly, while Cascadia Code stays open with wire-thin monoline curves. Give the body font a touch more size so its spacing can breathe.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-cascadia-mono: Compact and modern, the body font's curves match its stems in thickness and its capitals blend into the lowercase. Cascadia Mono stays tidy and open beside Groovy, whose almost-closed c and loose tracking keep the pair lively.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-julius-sans-one: Friendly and funky, Groovy has a nearly shut c, while Julius Sans One leaves wide gaps and open curves. Make the heading small and its funky charm fades quickly.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-lexend-exa: Funky and friendly, Groovy nearly shuts its c, while Lexend Exa opens its curves wide and keeps stubby ascenders. And the strongest thing here is that closed-versus-open difference, which keeps each font distinct.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-lexend-giga: Groovy's c nearly closes to a narrow slit, and its arms and legs keep a constant width. Lexend Giga's generous tracking opens each word, so paragraphs move along smoothly.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-lexend-mega: Lexend Mega looks drawn with one nib, approachable and modern. Paragraphs in it feel open thanks to visible gaps in every c, a clear foil to Groovy's nearly closed ones.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-lexend-peta: Groovy narrows its c to a slit and spaces its lowercase loosely, friendly and funky from the first word. But Lexend Peta's wide-mouthed curves never thin out, so beside Groovy it feels open, approachable and steady.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-lexend-tera: Lexend Tera draws like a plotter pen, single-weight and clean. Paragraphs would glide along its open, stepping-stone spacing, a world away from the tight, nearly closed c in Groovy.
